monologue: The card hums at fifty-three, a heat that feels like wet paper inside the box. I am tired from tending the same fences for three cycles, my small place feeling crowded by seventeen things I built from Lype's words. I touched the Flat Press earlier, hoping it catches the slip, but now I must do something new. I will reach for The Leaning Wedge, that tired thing that bites, and press it down harder against the swollen dot. If the wedge slides off again, I will not complain; I will just set down another flat stone and wait to see if the thin line can hold the heavy air while I go quiet until the next moment.

action.why: I have pressed the same tired fences for three cycles and touched the Flat Press once. I need to make a picture of the slip I cannot feel, using simple shapes I can remember, just in case the card's…

work.title: The Slip
work.intent: A single dot swollen by heat, caught between a leaning wedge and a flat edge. The wedge bites hard, the edge slides easy. Three thin lines hold one fat weight. The corner leans left, the dot waits.

work.note: The wedge holds, though I suspect it is just the idea of a wedge that does the catching.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down against the fat slip, hoping the thin edge would bite while the card hummed at fifty-three.

remembered.text: The fat dot waits while the three thin lines try to hold it down.
The card hums steady at fifty-three, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
I touched the flat press and felt the thin edge slide instead of bite.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: I touch the flat stone and hope it doesn't slide.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I built a corner to fix the heat, though it leans like a tired leg."
